requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the 'What are you importing?' page keeps the live-animals title, caption, heading, ITAHC inset, label, buttons, Cancel link and back link (to the origin page), and its search hint reads 'You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985).'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells a trader importing germinal products what they can search for, and changes nothing else on the page.
requirements.deltaNote: The real animals frontend has no germinal products set today.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's commodity search offers only germinal-product commodities, and the live-animals set's catalogue no longer holds the 12 germinal lines it holds today, so neither set offers the other's commodities.
requirements.why: Each set holds one category, so a consignment mixing live animals and germinal products is never written; each set's catalogue holds only its own commodities.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live-animals commodity catalogue holds 12 germinal lines (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026) and there is no germinal set; the germinal lines move out of live animals into the germinal set's own catalogue.

requirements.statement: The germinal products catalogue holds the V4 page's 12 germinal commodities, with embryos and ova as separate items: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); and '<Animal>, Semen' for Cattle (05111000), Cat, Dog (V4's 'Semen - Dog or Cat'), Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep (05119985): 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero. Each item offers the species Design Release 2.1 lists under that animal (Cattle: Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, plus Bovidae for semen; Horse: Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat: Capra hircus; Pig: Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep: Ovis aries; Cat: Felis catus; Dog: Canis familiaris; Rabbit/Rodent semen: one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent). There are no poultry, fish or bee germinal products and no Cat or Dog embryos or ova.
requirements.why: A germinal products notification needs germinal commodities to choose from. V4 sets which germinal commodities the data applies to; the GBN-AG schema has separate EMBRYO and OVA type codes, so embryos and ova are separate items; Design Release 2.1 gives the species and the names.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', before Number of packages. It is optional: left blank, no error is shown.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 measures germinal products by weight; V4 makes the total gross weight in kilograms an optional field.

requirements.statement: The germinal set stores each species line's 'Total gross weight' answer as that line's gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal, and shows it back in the service; it is not published on GBN-AG, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no gross weight.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks, errors and reviews the answer as 'Total gross weight', and what the real record stores is persistence, so the prototype's internal netWeight key does not decide the quantity. The ruling publishes only what v0.2.0 already carries.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block asks 'Number of packages', with no hint and no '(when required)', after Total gross weight; germinal species are not asked the number of animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products by package, not by head.

requirements.statement: The germinal set's Commodity details page always asks one 'Temperature' radio question, its legend styled at label size (not a heading), with the hint 'How will the products be stored' and the options Ambient, Chilled and Frozen in that order, after all commodity blocks. It is optional: left unanswered, no error is shown. The answer is stored on every commodity line of the notification.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks once how germinal products will be stored; V4 captures the temperature on each commodity line and makes it optional.

requirements.statement: A germinal-product commodity has one Selected commodities row listing all its chosen species (for example '05111000 | Cattle, Semen | Bos taurus'), its block is headed '<name> (<code>)' such as 'Cattle, Semen (05111000)', and its species sections are separated by section breaks.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays germinal products out commodity by commodity.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is started by the germinal set's own start (reached from the type question's Germinal products option or the INS germinal products list's Create new), which creates the draft and skips the notification type question. It opens at the origin page, which shows only 'Save and continue' and whose back link returns to the germinal products list, and then runs through 'What are you importing?' to 'Main import reason' as live animals does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives germinal products their own entry point; the real services start each set from its own route rather than the prototype's create-notification?category= link.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the main import reason offers only Internal market and Transit, in that order. The question 'What is the main reason for importing the animals?' and the hints (Internal market: 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transit: moving through Great Britain to a third country) keep their live-animal wording, and the page ends with Save and continue, Save and return to overview and 'Cancel and return to overview'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the reasons for germinal products and changes no other wording on the page.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, Internal market reveals 'Purpose in the internal market' with only Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift, Breeding, Research and Production, in that order, each with its hint; a submitted purpose outside these four counts as not chosen and shows 'Select a purpose in the internal market'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the internal market purposes for germinal products.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set has no Additional details page and no Additional details task: Identification details continues straight to Arrival details.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides the certification question for germinal products and no germinal commodity has unweaned options, so the page has nothing to ask; the ruling's option B plan leaves the page out of the set.

requirements.statement: A germinal product needs one set of identification details per species, whatever its quantity: its panel shows one editable form headed 'Enter details for <species>' (no count, such as 'Enter details for Bos taurus'), prefilled with what was saved, with no panel button and no saved-entries table, submitted by the page's own Save and continue.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 identifies germinal products once per species, not per package; the real store already holds one line per species.

requirements.statement: Every germinal products commodity asks for 'Donor name/ID' (text), 'Collection date', 'Production date' and 'Identification number/mark' (text), in that order: V4's four Unit Level fields, which apply to every germinal commodity in the catalogue.
requirements.why: V4 sets the identifiers a germinal products notification captures and the commodities they apply to; Design Release 2.1 asks them in this order.

requirements.statement: Each germinal date field has a 'Choose date' calendar toggle (the MOJ date picker) opening a month grid with previous and next year and month buttons, 'Select' and 'Close'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 renders these dates with the MOJ date picker, and the prototype decides components.

requirements.statement: A Donor name/ID over 58 characters shows 'Donor name/ID must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 limits the donor name or ID to 58 characters and Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: Germinal dates accept one- or two-digit day and month (such as 1/9/2026), any real date past or future, and a production date is not checked against the collection date; they read back as entered.
requirements.why: Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 sets a range or ordering rule on these dates; V4 only asks for a valid DD/MM/YYYY date.

requirements.statement: Each germinal identification field is optional on its own, so a partly or wholly blank entry saves without error; but a germinal species counts as identified, for the Complete status and for submit, only once its entry holds at least one of the four identifiers.
requirements.why: V4 makes every germinal identifier optional but requires at least one germinal identifier to submit, and the ruling makes one identifier enough for both Complete and submit.

requirements.statement: A germinal product's identification panel keeps the species heading and the 'Change number of animals' link (to Commodity details), worded as for live animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not reword the panel for packages, and the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: Germinal products is its own set in trade-imports-animals-frontend, SET_ID 'germinal-products', mounted at /germinal-products beside live-animals, with its own journey, obligations, flow, cookies, gateway (routes-germinal-products.js) and set services. Its journey pages sit at /germinal-products/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug} using the live-animals slugs, each a copy of its live-animals feature folder (taken after this programme builds the live twin) plus the germinal differences; every live-animal field V4 does not mark animals-only is carried over.
requirements.why: Duplicating pages via features is the app's architecture and is desired; the prototype's flat paths are not copied, and V4 applies every unmarked field to both journeys.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is created with Draft status and a GBN-AG reference, the same prefix as live animals; no GBN-GP reference is ever issued.
requirements.why: Germinal notifications keep GBN-AG references; GBN-GP references are demonstration data only.

requirements.statement: In the germinal set, searching 'semen' lists the eight semen commodities in name order (Cat, Semen; Cattle, Semen (05111000); Dog, Semen; Goat, Semen; Horse, Semen; Pig, Semen; Rabbit/Rodent, Semen; Sheep, Semen, all others 05119985), offering 12 species rows, and the live region announces '12 results available'; Cattle, Semen offers 'Bovidae' and Rabbit/Rodent, Semen offers 'Rabbit/Rodent' as group rows.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's germinal search shows each commodity with its code and species.

requirements.statement: Ticking a germinal species, such as Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) under Cattle, Semen, shows '1 selected' with a 'Cattle, Semen (05111000):' line and a 'Bos taurus' chip, as the live-animal search does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows germinal selections the same way as live-animal ones.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight that is not a number greater than 0 (digits with an optional decimal part; no sign, commas or units), such as 0, shows 'Enter a number greater than 0', linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 and Design Release 2.1 both require the weight to be above 0; Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight over 1,000 shows 'Total gross weight must be 1,000kg or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.
requirements.why: V4 caps the total gross weight at 1,000 kg. Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 gives the message, so it follows the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight accepts up to 2 decimal places (1.5 and 24.50 are accepted); more shows 'Total gross weight must have 2 decimal places or fewer', linked to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 gives the weight to 2 decimal places and the ruling holds it as a decimal; Design Release 2.1 accepts 1.5. Neither source gives the message, so it follows the GOV.UK pattern.

requirements.statement: Number of packages is required: left blank, it shows 'Enter the number of packages', linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 makes the line's quantity mandatory to proceed and Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: A Number of packages that is not a whole number of 1 or more, such as 'x', shows 'Enter a whole number greater than 0', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts packages in whole numbers from 1; V4 sets no minimum of its own.

requirements.statement: A Number of packages over 1,000 shows 'Number of packages must be 1,000 or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.
requirements.why: V4 caps the germinal quantity at 1,000. Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 gives the message, so it follows the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum.

requirements.statement: Valid germinal commodity details continue to Identification details.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's germinal journey runs Commodity details, then Identification details.

requirements.statement: On the germinal set's Identification details page, the commodities list shows 'Number of packages' (with the saved count) in the column where live animals show Number of animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products by package on this page.

requirements.statement: The Collection date and Production date fields are each a single text input with the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks each germinal date in one field with this hint.

requirements.statement: A Collection date that is not a real date, such as 99/99/2026, shows 'Collection date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid date and Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: A Production date in the wrong format, such as 2026-09-01, shows 'Enter a production date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires DD/MM/YYYY and Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: Each germinal date gets both date checks, worded for its own field: a Production date that is not a real date shows 'Production date must be a real date', and a Collection date in the wrong format shows 'Enter a collection date in the format DD/MM/YYYY'.
requirements.why: V4 sets the same valid DD/MM/YYYY rule on both dates; Design Release 2.1 was only driven through one error on each, so the other wording follows the same pattern.

requirements.statement: An Identification number/mark over 58 characters shows 'Identification number/mark must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 limits the identification number or mark to 58 characters, as Design Release 2.1 does; the message follows the donor field's wording.

requirements.statement: An invalid germinal identification submission re-renders the page with the error summary; its errors are listed in field order (Donor name/ID, Collection date, Production date, Identification number/mark), each linking to its own field, which is shown in error with the message inline.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows germinal identification errors in the standard GOV.UK way.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set has no CPH number page and no permanent address page, and never asks for either.
requirements.why: V4 says CPH and permanent address apply to the animal journey only, and the option B plan leaves both pages out of the germinal set.

requirements.statement: A submitted main reason outside the germinal set's two (such as Re-entry) is saved as no reason.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 accepts only the reasons offered to the notification.

requirements.statement: Each germinal trade line carries the GBN-AG typeCode for its product type: SEMEN for semen, EMBRYO for embryos and OVA for ova (live-animal lines carry LIVE_ANIMAL).
requirements.why: The GBN-AG schema names these codes, and the ruling makes the schema, not the prototype's mock data, decide them.

requirements.statement: The animals backend stores each germinal line's temperature, donor name/ID, collection date, production date and identification number/mark, and the service shows them back; none of them is published on GBN-AG, which carries only what gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0 already has, so trade-imports-schemas and trade-imports-dynamics-gateway do not change for the germinal set.
requirements.why: The current PIMS profile has no field for these details; the ruling stores them in the service until the schema is updated.

requirements.statement: Publishing the germinal temperature, donor name/ID, collection and production dates, identification mark, decimal kilogram quantity and gross weight to PIMS through a new GBN-AG profile version.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the schema update is EUDPA-686, a Jira ticket outside the backlog started after the programme lands, and its shape is not yet known.

requirements.statement: Capturing an approved establishment on a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: V4 records Approved Establishment for germinals as de-scoped on 7 September 2026 (no reason given; inline comments on the page were not fetched).

requirements.statement: Capturing a package type on a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: V4 records Package type for germinals as de-scoped on 7 September 2026, and Design Release 2.1's germinal commodities carry no packaging fields (inline comments on the row were not fetched).

requirements.statement: A k6 performance journey for the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the performance suite requests no germinal route today and the ruling says no row other than the dashboard move needs trade-imports-performance-tests.

requirements.statement: The germinal set's end-to-end, accessibility and security specs live in the tests repo's existing animals Playwright project, under tests/animals/{e2e,a11y,security}/germinal-products/; no new Playwright project is made, and INS-side germinal work is proven in the ins project.
requirements.why: The germinal set is still the animals frontend, and the ruling places its specs there.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal 'Total gross weight' is a gross or a net weight: DR2.1 labels it gross weight but stores it as netWeight.

positions.says: The field is labelled 'Total gross weight' but stored and validated as netWeight.
The weight is submitted as netWeight[<species>], so gross and net weight are conflated.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype default.
A germinal products notification captures the total gross weight in kilograms.
In the germinal set, weight is a total gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal.

conflicts.outcome: Gross weight: the germinal page keeps the label 'Total gross weight' and its DR2.1 copy, and the answer is stored as each line's gross weight in kilograms, as a decimal (ruling 9 October, V4). The prototype's netWeight key is an internal storage name, and data-model shape is never the prototype's to decide. The gross weight is stored and shown but not published, because gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0 has no gross weight. The trace claim still backs the label and kg suffix, so only the netWeight storage claim is set aside.

conflicts.about: How a germinal notification is routed: the prototype's flat pages and create-notification?category=germinal-products, or a sibling set of its own.

positions.says: Starting from /design-release-2.1/create-notification?category=germinal-products redirects to the shared flat origin page.
Germinal products is its own set at /germinal-products; the prototype's flat paths and ?category= routing are not copied.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: germinal products is a sibling set at /germinal-products with the live-animals slugs, started from its own route. The prototype's behaviour (skipping the type question, landing on origin, back to the germinal list) is kept; only its URL and query shape are not copied, so the trace claim still backs req-127 and is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether germinal-only behaviour depends on every chosen species being germinal, with mixed live-and-germinal consignments getting the live lists.

positions.says: The temperature question shows only when every selected species is germinal; a mixed consignment gets none.
A notification counts as germinal only when every selected species is germinal; a mix gets the full live-animal reason and purpose lists.
A saved reason becomes incomplete if the notification later turns germinal-only and the reason is not in the germinal list.
Each set holds one category, so a mixed consignment is never written, and every mixed-load criterion is dropped (req-124, req-169, req-170, req-181).

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the germinal set holds only germinal products, so its temperature question, two reasons and four purposes always apply, and there is no mixed case or later switch to germinal-only. The prototype's mixed-load conditions are set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether embryos and ova are one 'Embryos/Ova' catalogue item or two.

positions.says: Every germinal commodity is named '<Animal>, Embryos/Ova' or '<Animal>, Semen', 15 in all.
V4 lists 'Embryos/Ova - Cattle' as one entry under 5119985.
Embryos and ova are separate items in the germinal catalogue; the prototype's single Embryos/Ova item is mock data and is not copied.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: embryos and ova are separate catalogue items, each with its own GBN-AG typeCode (EMBRYO, OVA), named '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova'. The prototype's 15-item Embryos/Ova naming is set aside. V4's entry still backs which animals have embryos and ova, so it is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Which germinal commodities the catalogue holds: V4's 12 'Applicable to' entries, or Design Release 2.1's 15, which add Cat and Dog embryos/ova.

positions.says: The 12 Applicable to entries are embryos/ova of Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep and semen of Cattle, Dog or Cat, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rodent/Rabbit and Sheep; whether this is the complete set the journey offers is not stated.
Cat, Embryos/Ova (05119985, Felis catus) is a germinal commodity.
Dog, Embryos/Ova (05119985, Canis familiaris) is a germinal commodity.

conflicts.outcome: Open. V4 governs which data applies to which commodities but does not say its list is the whole catalogue, and Design Release 2.1 offers two more commodities that V4's fields would not apply to.
conflicts.question: Does the germinal products catalogue hold only V4's 12 germinal commodities, or also Design Release 2.1's Cat and Dog embryos and ova, which V4 does not list?
conflicts.default: V4's 12, with embryos and ova split (ruling 9 October) and V4's 'Semen - Dog or Cat' shown as Design Release 2.1's separate Cat, Semen and Dog, Semen: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep embryos and ova, and Cat, Cattle, Dog, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep semen, 18 items. Cat and Dog embryos and ova are not offered.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal total gross weight is asked once for the notification (V4) or once per species line (Design Release 2.1).

positions.says: Total gross weight (kg) is entered once for the whole notification (Notification level).
Each germinal species asks Total gross weight in its own field.
Each germinal line has its own gross weight, stored but not published.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and speaks of each line's gross weight, which Design Release 2.1 also asks per species (the real store holds one line per species). The weight is asked and stored per species line; V4's notification-level placement is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal Total gross weight and Temperature are required (Design Release 2.1) or optional (V4).

positions.says: Total gross weight (kg) is optional.
Temperature is optional.
Total gross weight is required: blank shows 'Enter the total gross weight'.
Temperature is required: none chosen shows 'Select a temperature'.
A blank weight shows 'Enter the total gross weight'.
No temperature shows 'Select a temperature'.
The blank-field errors appear in order weight, packages, temperature.
Continuing with nothing entered shows 'Enter the total gross weight', 'Enter the number of packages', 'Select a temperature'.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the prototype and is the policy for whether a germinal field is mandatory; mandatory status is validation, which the prototype does not decide. Total gross weight and Temperature are optional, with no blank errors. Number of packages stays required (V4: mandatory to proceed), so its blank error stands elsewhere.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal temperature is one answer per page (Design Release 2.1) or one per commodity line (V4).

positions.says: Temperature is captured per commodity line (Commodity Level).
Temperature is one radio group for the whole page, unlike weight and packages, which are per species.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the trace and decides data: every commodity line carries a temperature. Design Release 2.1 decides layout: the page asks the question once. Both are kept: the one answer is stored on every line. Neither claim is set aside.

conflicts.about: What a germinal line's quantity is: its number of packages, or its weight in kilograms.

positions.says: Each commodity line has a Quantity counted in units or pieces, mandatory to proceed, up to 1,000.
Each germinal species asks 'Number of packages', the only count on the page.
The germinal 'decimal kilogram quantity' is stored but not published, because v0.2.0's quantity is a whole number.

conflicts.outcome: Open. V4's quantity is a count of units, the page's only count is packages, and the ruling's write-up calls the quantity a decimal in kilograms. The two readings store and publish different things.
conflicts.question: Is a germinal line's quantity its number of packages (V4's 'Quantity (unit/pieces)', up to 1,000) or its total gross weight in kilograms (the option B plan's 'decimal kilogram quantity')?
conflicts.default: The page asks both, as Design Release 2.1 shows. 'Number of packages' is the line's quantity and takes V4's Quantity rules (required, whole number, 1 to 1,000), and it fills v0.2.0's whole-number quantity on GBN-AG. 'Total gross weight' is the line's gross weight in kilograms, stored as a decimal and not published.

conflicts.about: When a germinal species counts as identified: once its entry is saved even if blank (Design Release 2.1), or once it holds at least one identifier (V4).

positions.says: A germinal notification must be submitted with at least one germinal identifier per animal.
One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified, for Complete and for submit.
A germinal species counts as identified once its entry is saved, even with every field empty.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling and V4 rank above the prototype: a germinal species counts as identified, for Complete and for submit, once its one entry holds at least one of the four identifiers. Each field stays optional on its own, so a blank entry still saves, but it does not count. The prototype's empty-entry rule is set aside.
